newsitem.title: USA: GE says on track for record results in 1997.
newsitem.headline: GE says on track for record results in 1997.

text.p: General Electric Co said Thursday it was poised to post record earnings for the full year 1997.

The forecast came as the company reported the highest quarterly earnings in its history -- second quarter earnings of $2.2 billion, or $0.66 a share, compared with $1.9 billion, or $0.58 a share, a year earlier.
According to First Call, analysts' consensus estimate for the second quarter was $0.65 a share.
"These strong second-quarter results position GE to deliver another year of record performance in 1997," said Chairman John Welch in a statement.

GE said earnings per share grew faster (up 14 percent) than earnings (up 13 percent) in the second quarter, reflecting the effect of a four-year, $13 billion share buyback program started in December 1994.
The company attributed the 15 percent rise in revenues to $22.0 billion to increased global activities and higher sales of spare parts and services by its equipment businesses.
GE said its operating margin increased to a record 17.1 percent in the second quarter, up from the year-earlier 16.3 percent.

The company said 10 of its 12 businesses reported higher operating profit for the second quarter, with nine -- led by GE Capital Services, NBC and Aircraft Engines -- achieving double-digit increases.

GE Capital Services's earnings were $798 million, up 17 percent from last year's $683 million. The strong rise was attributed to double-digit increases in specialty insurance, equipment management and mid-market financing activities.

GE Capital made 11 acquisitions in the second quarter, in Austria, Brazil, the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Portugal and the UK. The division also made inroads in the car insurance business -- it agreed to buy auto insurer Colonial Penn P&C Group from Leucadia National Corp for $950 million cash on June 30.

GE said its Aircraft Engines division won more than 70 percent of large commercial engine orders in 1997. It also won several large multi-year engine service agreements, including a 10-year, $1.6 billion contract from Southwest Airlines Co, GE said.
GE Power Systems won three additional multi-year power plant service agreements, pushing the value of its 1997 service awards over $1 billion, the company said.

In other corporate developments, GE said its plastics division formed a new joint venture with Bayer AG, and its appliances business introduced a new appliance product line and new water filtration and softening products.

GE said it generated $3.5 billion in cash from operating activities the first half of 1997, equaling last year's level but up sharply if several unusual receipts are excluded from the year-ago number.

The company said it bought back $862 million of its stock in the second quarter, bringing the buyback total to $8.1 billion, or 218 million shares, since December 1994, when it started the repurchase program.
GE's stock traded at 69-1/4 this morning, up 13/16 and close to its 52-week high of 70-14/16.
"At the halfway point of the year, GE is on track to deliver record results to its shareholders in 1997," Welch said.
